Thanks — quick recommendations based on their uploaded traffic patterns and model mix:

1) Region: us-west1 (best availability for A100/H100; single-region is fine initially). Add a passive us-east replica for multi-region failover if they require SLA-backed geo-redundancy.

2) GPU family & sizing: for their model classes (mix of 13B decoder + a smaller reranker), recommend a mix: 2x H100 80GB for low-latency production routing + 6x A100s in a separate burst pool to cover large batches. This gives predictable p95s and cost flexibility.

3) Autoscale & burst template:
- Steady pool: reserved pool sized for 130 rps capacity (10% headroom).
- Burst pool: elastic autoscale with target CPU/GPU utilization trigger at 65% and a token-bucket burst allowance to allow 2.5x baseline for up to 15 minutes.
- Warm pool: maintain a small hot-standby of pre-warmed kernels (10% of steady capacity) to shave cold-starts.
- Prewarm strategy: scale up burst instances 5 min before scheduled batch windows (via calendar hooks) and allow immediate on-demand for unexpected spikes with degraded QoS fallback (lower precision quantized model).

4) KV cache / warm times: initial KV-cache warm for typical conversations ~2-3s per request on H100; warm-up of kernels after scale events ~30-90s depending on model and quantization. Plan canaries of 10-15% traffic for 24-48h with traffic shadowing to validate latency & correctness.

5) Observability & SLOs: enable per-route token-level latency histograms and deploy a canary that runs synthetic prompt set every 5 min; connect alerts to pager for sustained p95 > 400ms for >5m.

I can draft a concrete autoscale policy config (yaml) and suggested instance counts ahead of Thu9s call if you want.

—Rishi
